messages:
maya: quick sync — i'm drafting the PRD/RFC for token ownership & visibility (api keys, scoped tokens, org/project mapping). wanted to capture acceptance criteria and migration plan before i open the GH draft. agenda: token types + owner semantics, console visibility + logs, rb ac mapping, migration path. any must-haves?
aj: +1. big ask: do not leak org/project identifiers in publicly-accessible logs or URLs. acceptance should include: scrubbed logs by default + opt-in verbose for internal audit only.
liam: FYI Acme Customer asked for project-scoped service tokens that contractors can use. key requirements: scope to single project, optional read-only flag, and ability to rotate without breaking existing deployments.
sasha: also need strong audit mapping: every token creation must record creator_id, creator_role, org_id, project_ids, and an immutable token_id for tracing. acceptance: console shows last_used_by + last_used_at.
maya: draft acceptance criteria i'm thinking of (short):
- token types: user-api-key, service-token (scoped), legacy-api-key (backcompat)
- ownership: tokens tie to owner_id (user or service principal) and org_id; project_ids is optional list for scoped tokens
- visibility: UI shows masked value; full token only shown once at creation; logs store token_id (not raw token)
- RBAC: project-scoped tokens inherit project-level permissions by policy evaluation; admins can list all tokens for their org
- rotation: creating new token can optionally replace old token id with atomic swap; revocation should be immediate
- audit: token creation/rotation/revocation events logged with actor_id and ip

example minimal token object:
```json
{"token_id":"tk_01F...","owner_id":"usr_123","org_id":"org_9","project_ids":["proj_a"],"type":"service","created_at":"2026-06-20T14:12:00Z"}
```
aj: question: do we need default project fallback? e.g., token created from org-level UI without explicit project should be org-scoped. if a user creates from project page, default to that project. failure modes?
liam: agree — default should be explicit. edge-case: token created via API with missing project_ids — return 400 unless caller is org-admin and passes allow_org_scope flag. record that in acceptance criteria.
sasha: migration path for legacy-api-keys: backfill token_id for existing rows, set owner_id from created_by, and mark legacy tokens as org-scoped unless we detect project metadata. rollout: canary with 3 beta customers, then org-wide migration script with incremental revocation option.
maya: rollout acceptance: no more than 0.1% increase in 5xx on token auth path during canary, and telemetry must confirm audit events emitted for >99.9% of token ops. document rollback plan in PRD.
aj: schema note — we probably need an additional column token_id (uuid), project_ids as jsonb, owner_type enum. estimate of db migration: non-blocking, backfill in background. confirm with infra.
liam: small edge-case: when project is deleted, tokens scoped to that project should either be disabled or moved to orphaned-project state with alert. which do we want?
sasha: prefer disable + notify owner. acceptance: deletion triggers token disable and email to creator and org-admins.
maya: ok next steps: i'll open RFC draft by EOD with the acceptance criteria above and a proposed DB migration script + migration runbook. owners: maya (PRD + RFC), aj (privacy/logging review), sasha (audit + rollout), liam (customer impact + migration testing).
deploy-bot: created issue #4128: "RFC: token ownership & visibility" and linked to milestone "auth-q3" :rocket:
maya: thanks — will ping here when draft is up, please add any specific edge-cases you want included (e.g., cross-org token sharing, short-lived ephemeral tokens use-cases).
